places.name: Ajloun Forest Reserve
places.address: Ajloun highlands, Ajloun Governorate, northern Jordan; reference pin for the forest reserve, not a surveyed entrance.
places.description:
Ajloun Forest Reserve offers a woodland visit in the northern Jordanian highlands. Evergreen oak and other Mediterranean trees shelter wildlife, while walking routes introduce the reserve's landscape and nearby rural communities. RSCN manages the reserve, and UNESCO's biosphere programme records the wider Ajloun designation in 2025.

Visitors can consider the short Roe Deer Trail or ask about guided routes connecting woodland with local craft enterprises. The Soap House, Biscuit House and Calligraphy House illustrate how conservation and community livelihoods are linked. These are distinct experiences with their own arrangements, not activities guaranteed with every admission. Spring is noted for wildflowers. Confirm the chosen route, guide requirements, fees and access with the operator before travelling. An editorial planning allowance of two to four hours suits a short reserve visit, rather than a full-day guided itinerary. Step-free access has not been verified.
places.best_time_to_visit: Spring for woodland greenery and wildflowers; confirm trail conditions with RSCN.
places.transportation_notes: Use the forest reserve location reference, not Ajloun Castle. Confirm arrival, parking and any guided-route transfers with RSCN. No driving-time or step-free-access guarantee is provided.

places.name: Dana Biosphere Reserve
places.address: Dana village reference area, Tafilah Governorate, Jordan; choose the appropriate trailhead separately for the wider reserve.
places.description:
Dana Biosphere Reserve spans mountain slopes and deep valleys towards Wadi Araba, bringing together markedly different habitats in a compact landscape. Managed by RSCN, it combines biodiversity conservation with nature tourism and local livelihoods. Dana village offers a cultural introduction through its older buildings, terraced gardens and craft activity, while the reserve's walking routes reach very different terrain.

Choose an itinerary before travelling: a village walk is not equivalent to a long descent into Wadi Dana or a visit to Feynan. The Jordan Tourism Board describes both guided and self-guided options, with some routes requiring a licensed guide or operating only in a stated season. RSCN's 2026 trail list separates route durations and notes that some transfers cost extra. Confirm the starting point, return transport, weather and guide arrangements. No single duration, admission price or universal accessibility claim is supplied for the entire reserve. The saved pin is a Dana reference area, not its boundary or a surveyed entrance.
places.transportation_notes: Confirm your chosen starting point and return transfer with RSCN. A descent towards Feynan requires a return or onward plan; the Dana village reference pin does not locate every trail. The 2026 operator list notes extra transport costs for some routes.

places.name: Iraq Al-Amir
places.address: Iraq Al-Amir area southwest of Amman, Jordan; Qasr El-Abd is a separate monument within the wider visit.
places.description:
Iraq Al-Amir offers a heritage visit southwest of Amman, where olive-growing countryside, hillside caves and ancient stone architecture form a different setting from the city centre. The Jordan Tourism Board identifies nearby Qasr El-Abd as a rare surviving example of pre-Roman architecture in Jordan, dating to the second century BCE. Its substantial masonry makes it a focus for visitors interested in the region's archaeological landscape.

Treat the area and the palace as related but distinct places when planning a route. The local women's cooperative adds a contemporary craft connection, with visits requiring their own arrangements. Allow one to two hours as an editorial suggestion for an introductory archaeological stop, extending the visit only if other activities are arranged. Confirm access, opening and the appropriate arrival point before travelling. Cave access, step-free routes and current transport services have not been verified. The saved reference point is for the area rather than a surveyed palace entrance.
places.transportation_notes: Plan arrival in the Iraq Al-Amir area separately from access to Qasr El-Abd or the women's cooperative. Confirm the intended stop locally; the map reference is not a verified palace entrance. No driving time or public-bus timetable is asserted.

places.name: As-Salt Historic Centre
places.address: Historic urban core of As-Salt, Balqa highlands, west-central Jordan; UNESCO property reference point, not a parking or entrance pin.
places.description:
As-Salt's historic centre brings together yellow-limestone buildings, connected stairways, narrow lanes and public spaces on steep hills. Its late-Ottoman growth as a trading town shaped an architecture and urban culture recognised by UNESCO when the property was inscribed in 2021. The listing highlights both the built environment and traditions of hospitality and cooperation among Muslim and Christian communities.

A visit is best approached as a walk through a living urban district, with time to look at stonework, streets and the relationships between neighbourhoods and shared spaces. Respect homes, worship and everyday activity; private buildings are not automatically visitor attractions. Allow two to three hours as an editorial suggestion for an introductory walk. Stairways and changes in level are integral to the townscape, so visitors needing step-free access should confirm a suitable route locally. Individual museums and buildings have separate access arrangements; no single admission price or opening calendar is verified for the whole district.
places.transportation_notes: Plan a walking route through the historic core and arrange an appropriate arrival point locally. The UNESCO property reference pin is not a verified car park. Stairways and steep streets mean step-free access must be checked for the intended route.

places.name: Umm Qais
places.address: Umm Qais archaeological site and Ottoman village, northern Jordan; official site-area reference, not a surveyed visitor entrance.
places.description:
At Umm Qais, the remains of ancient Gadara occupy a hilltop above the Jordan Valley. A colonnaded street, theatre remains and dark basalt architecture give visitors an introduction to a city associated with the Decapolis. The Ottoman-era village occupies part of the ancient site, adding another layer to the landscape.

The museum is housed in an Ottoman-period building and presents archaeological finds from the area, including ceramics and sculpture. An introductory visit can combine the archaeological remains, village setting and museum rather than treating the modern town as the attraction itself. Allow two to three hours as an editorial recommendation, subject to the areas open on the day. Check current hours, ticket eligibility and museum access before travelling; official pages do not provide a fully consistent operating schedule. The saved point is a site-area reference shared by official tourism links, not a confirmed entrance. Step-free access and current visitor facilities require local confirmation.
places.transportation_notes: Use the archaeological-site reference and confirm the visitor arrival point locally. Official seasonal and attraction-summary hours differ, so confirm site and museum opening before departure. No driving time, bus service or step-free route is guaranteed.

places.name: Mujib Biosphere Reserve
places.address: Mujib Adventure Center reference area by the Dead Sea Highway, eastern Dead Sea shore, Jordan; not the centre of the whole reserve.
places.description:
Mujib Biosphere Reserve protects a striking transition between the Dead Sea shore and the surrounding mountain country. Its valleys, cliffs and river habitats support a varied natural landscape. A visit to the reserve is not one interchangeable activity: water routes and dry-land hikes have different seasons, requirements and booking arrangements.

The Siq Trail starts from Mujib Adventure Center and follows the river through a sandstone gorge towards a waterfall. Water levels can require swimming, and access depends on weather and the operator's safety decisions. RSCN's 2026 trail list gives two to three hours for the self-guided Siq route and a separate guided Ibex option. Earlier RSCN operating guidance sets a minimum age of 18 for wet trails; reconfirm current eligibility before booking. Do not assume a published season guarantees same-day access. The saved point represents the Adventure Center reference area, not a surveyed entrance or the reserve's full extent. Current opening and individual accessibility must be checked with RSCN.
places.best_time_to_visit: Water trails are seasonal and weather dependent. Confirm current opening and safety conditions with RSCN; a calendar season is not an access guarantee.
places.transportation_notes: Arrange arrival at the Mujib Adventure Center reference area for the Siq route. Other trails may use different starting points or require a guide and transfers. Confirm the selected activity with RSCN; no journey time is assumed.
